npcs.name: Court Singer Shahra
npcs.greet: Shahra sings the hours of the Mane's Court: Masser's hour, Secunda's hour, and the held-breath hour when neither moon is up. People forget a singer is in the room. Shahra remembers everything they said.

npcs.name: Mane's Scribe Jaro
npcs.greet: Jaro keeps the lunar ledger and has ink to the elbow. He rises at moonset, eats at moonrise, and has not seen a noon since the harvest tax of three years ago.

npcs.name: Sugar-Duty Warden Ri'dar
npcs.greet: Ri'dar weighs every sack that enters the Exchange. He can tell a short measure by the sound it makes in the scale pan, and he is not shy about letting the seller hear it.

npcs.name: Ma'tisha of the Purring Ledger
npcs.greet: Welcome to the Purring Ledger. Ma'tisha keeps every tab in pawprints, not numbers, so no one can say she cheated them. She only has to remember whose paw is whose. She is very good at paws.

npcs.name: Cub-Runner Tazhi
npcs.greet: Tazhi runs notes between the Exchange, the Court and the Observatory for a copper each. Tazhi has read none of them. Tazhi has read all of them.

npcs.name: Master Artisan Kahlil
npcs.greet: Kahlil has made rings for three Princes and a spoon for a cat who outlived all of them. He is the finest hand in Rimmen and he will tell you so while you are in the middle of a sentence.

npcs.name: Gatewarden Sira
npcs.greet: Sira holds the key to the necropolis door and has never once lent it. The dead of Rimmen are her family. She is very particular about visitors, and she does not care how they are dressed.

npcs.name: Prince-Advisor Lek
npcs.greet: Lek advises the Prince on matters of trade, war and marriage. He advises on the weather, too, but only as a courtesy to the weather.

npcs.name: Tamhir of the Sugar Bowl
npcs.greet: The Sugar Bowl is a bowl-shaped courtyard tavern and Tamhir is its famous single employee. He pours, cooks, sweeps and sings. Ask for the house wine only if you are prepared to ask what is in it.

npcs.name: Customs-Master Ja'khar
npcs.greet: Ja'khar inspects every crate, barrel and bucket that crosses the Senchal quay. He once confiscated a sack of flour because it smelled "ambitious".

npcs.name: Boiler Tema
npcs.greet: Tema runs the third boiling-floor of the Sugar Boil House. Her forearms are burn-scarred to the elbow and she calls each vat by a name. They are all named after exes.

npcs.name: Prince's Cousin Rhal
npcs.greet: Rhal is the Prince's cousin, which he mentions in the first sentence, the second, and the invoice. He is generous, never on time, and always about to do you a favour that costs you money.

npcs.name: Zhaleh of the Sweet Breezes
npcs.greet: The Sweet Breezes is a three-storey inn where every room faces the sea and every window has been broken at least once by a wind that insists on coming in. Zhaleh swears the wind pays for its own glass.

npcs.name: Wheel-Master Khir
npcs.greet: Khir collects the toll at the hub of the Great Market Wheel. Every lane pays him a copper a cart, and every cart tries to look as if it has paid already. He has never once been fooled, and he is still annoyed about it.

npcs.name: Camel-Driver Mizra
npcs.greet: Mizra knows the roads of Anequina by the smell of their dust. She can tell you which oasis has gone bad by the way the camels refuse to look at it.

npcs.name: Fortune-Teller Nuri
npcs.greet: Nuri tells fortunes in a striped tent and has never been wrong, which is exactly why she is not very popular. She always tells you more than you paid for. She says it is a flaw in her scales.

npcs.name: Shakhra of the Eighth Spoke
npcs.greet: The Eighth Spoke stands on the eighth lane of the Wheel, which most visitors will tell you does not exist. It does. It is just always hidden behind the seventh. Shakhra pours from a skin on a hook and never repeats a drink twice the same way.

npcs.name: Water-Seller Hajir
npcs.greet: Hajir sells cups of water from a rolling barrel and a very small bell. He sells the same cup four times a day. He swears the water is fresher each time. It probably is.

npcs.name: Gardener-Priest Mura
npcs.greet: Mura tends the Garden Cathedral and its three hundred hives. She wears a veil of fine mesh and answers to the hum of her bees before she answers to her name.

npcs.name: Boatman Ajh
npcs.greet: Ajh poles a long canal-boat between the arching bridges and hums off-key. He knows every sluice, every bridge-ghost and which canal-side window to avoid after midnight.

npcs.name: Matron Zhel of the Orchard Hall
npcs.greet: Zhel is matron of the orchard guild and keeps the grafting-book that no one else is allowed to read. She is courteous, firm, and in thirty years has never once been caught telling the truth about a pear.

npcs.name: Skipper Rha'ni of the Green Barge
npcs.greet: The Green Barge is a moored river-barge that has been a tavern for eleven years and has not left its moorings in nine. Rha'ni swears it is still ready to sail. The barge, privately, is not so sure.

npcs.name: Bee-Cub Ji'sha
npcs.greet: Ji'sha has been stung more than anyone in Corinthe and counts it as a rank. She will tell you how many stings she has, which hive, and what the bee was thinking.

npcs.name: Gate-Captain Raz
npcs.greet: Raz commands the Claw Gate and is not a cat who smiles. He has a scar from ear to jaw and will explain it, in detail, if you ask nicely. No one has asked nicely.

npcs.name: Cistern-Keeper Mala
npcs.greet: Mala keeps the rooftop cisterns and has counted every drop that has fallen on Orcrest since she was a cub. She keeps the number in her head and tells it to no one.

npcs.name: Scout Sihe
npcs.greet: Sihe watches the plateau from the highest watchtower and says she can tell a bandit from a trader at four miles by how the dust sits. She is right more than seems fair.

npcs.name: Ruzhi of the Claw-and-Cistern
npcs.greet: The Claw-and-Cistern keeps a rain barrel in the middle of the taproom that is always full, even in drought. Ruzhi will not say why. She pours the best cold water in Anequina and charges for it like wine.

npcs.name: Ring-Keeper Dar
npcs.greet: Dar keeps the ring of moonstones in the centre of Hakoshae and sweeps it every dawn. He says the stones have never once been dirty, and he sweeps them anyway, because it is a courtesy.

npcs.name: Guardian Su'ri
npcs.greet: Su'ri is the tomb-guardian of the east side and carries a spear that has not once been used in anger. She says that is the whole point of a good spear.

npcs.name: Pilgrim Ke
npcs.greet: Ke has walked to every moon-temple of Elsweyr and is on his second lap. He has no goal. He says that is the pilgrimage.

npcs.name: Hamza of the Pilgrim's Rest
npcs.greet: Hamza runs the Pilgrim's Rest, a long low house with seventeen beds and no locks. He says the moonstones watch the door. Nobody has stolen anything from there in living memory, which is a long time among cats.

npcs.name: Balloonist Q'ri
npcs.greet: Q'ri pilots a balloon made from a grown netch and always has one story too many. She trades rides for tales. She trades tales for rides. She is rumoured to have no home on the ground at all.

npcs.name: Keeper Ma'tir of the Twin Moons
npcs.greet: Ma'tir runs the Twin Moons roadhouse where travellers wager on the moon-phase. She has lost every wager she ever made against the sky, and says it keeps the house honest.

npcs.name: Tathara the Cane-Widow
npcs.greet: Tathara grew sugar for thirty years. This season her fields burned in a night. She stands where the cane was and says nothing, and the neighbours know better than to ask.

npcs.name: Adept Zhazir
npcs.greet: Zhazir tutors three cubs in the stars beneath the adeptorium dome. A chart has gone missing, and he has been counting ceiling-tiles ever since to avoid saying so.

npcs.name: Route-Master Ha'bir
npcs.greet: Ha'bir carries the Baandari route book and counts sorry the day it was taken from his wagon. He is polite to everyone, and he counts their fingers.

relics.name: Tally-Stone of the Purifying Moons
relics.desc: A palm-sized disc of white clay scored with two columns of notches. One column counts casks sent out under the temple's seal, the other counts casks that came back. The columns have not matched in a year.

relics.name: Pawprint Tab-Book
relics.desc: Ma'tisha's oldest tab-book, thick with inked paw-pads. One long page of identical prints in pale grey ink records a moon-sugar run that no honest tavern should know about.

relics.name: Rubbing of the Tomb Mural
relics.desc: A charcoal rubbing on silk of a mural: a loom of seven strands, each strand a different Rimmen guild's sign, all seven woven into one pattern that no living artisan knows how to repeat.

relics.name: Sira's Loaned Key
relics.desc: A black iron key as long as a hand, warm from being carried against a priestess's heart. It opens the necropolis door, once.

relics.name: Phial of the Bitter Batch
relics.desc: A phial of cloudy sugar-syrup that tastes of sweet, then of iron, then of nothing at all. Three days of it make a dock-hand forget his own name.

relics.name: Tema's Boiler Token
relics.desc: A brass token stamped with a vat's number. Tema gives one to every hand she trusts to open the sluice. This one was found in the wrong boiler, three floors down.

relics.name: Bell of the Seventh Wagon
relics.desc: A brass caravan bell with a cracked lip, still warm. Its clapper has been tied with a strip of blue cloth, as if someone wished it to be quiet.

relics.name: Khir's Toll-Tally
relics.desc: A leather tally strap with a hundred knots. Each knot is a cart. One knot is a different colour, tied by someone who was not Khir.

relics.name: Queen Cell in a Wax Cradle
relics.desc: A sealed cradle of cream wax cut from the oldest hive of the Garden Cathedral. Inside, something very small is dreaming of flowers.

relics.name: Dwarven Honeycomb Cog
relics.desc: A palm-sized bronze cog, hexagonal, ringed with the faintest etched hive-pattern. It was made by people who clearly thought bees were showing off.

relics.name: Cracked Cistern Seal
relics.desc: A fired-clay seal that once bound the lid of the Third Cistern. A fingernail-wide crack runs across the face, and the crack is clean-edged: cut, not broken.

relics.name: Mala's Water-Ledger
relics.desc: A thick slate-bound ledger of every cistern's measure. The last four entries are written in a hand that is not Mala's.

relics.name: Alignment Lens of Hakoshae
relics.desc: A palm-sized disc of clear moonstone, polished flat on one side and curved on the other. Held up at the right hour, it throws both moons' light as one thin silver line across the ground.

relics.name: The Baandari Route Book
relics.desc: A leather-bound book of caravan routes drawn on goatskin, with wells, wolves and bribes marked in three colours of ink. Half the pages are written in a code only Baandari clans know.

relics.name: The Missing Star-Chart
relics.desc: A vellum star-chart of the winter sky, hand-lettered in silver ink. Someone has traced a seventh moon in faint pencil near the southern horizon.

relics.name: The Claw Gate Banner
relics.desc: A great saffron banner embroidered with a pair of black claws, folded over a rope. It is fraying at the edge where it was carried by someone in a hurry, and smells of rival-village woodsmoke.

relics.name: Moon-Cub's Charm
relics.desc: A little charm of two silver crescents on a thread, to be tied round a newborn's wrist at the first night when both moons show. This one has not yet been blessed.

relics.name: Cask of Blessed Moon-Sugar
relics.desc: A small oak cask sealed with the Moon-Priests' pawprint. It is faintly warm, and smells of honey and of something older. The seal has been pried and mended with wax.

mq_els_weaver_shade.name: The Weaver Who Would Not Stop

mq_els_tomb_tenant.name: The Tenant Beneath the Third Stone

mq_els_led_stones: Nine tally-stones sit in a ring on the shrine floor, each scored with notches for the moon-sugar casks blessed that season. Moonlight lies across them like a ruler.
Count them twice, walker. The temple says it blessed four hundred casks. The Exchange says it received three hundred and ninety-nine. One cask does not simply walk away on four legs.
mq_els_led_den: Barrels stamped with the temple seal are stacked behind a false wall of sugar-sacks. A cat with half a tail looks up from counting them and does not look worried.
A walker! Good. Ma'rish has been wanting someone to explain to the Mane why this is not stealing. It is... lending. To strangers. With interest.
mq_els_rim_mural: The necropolis mural is a loom the length of a hall. Seven bands of thread-pattern run into one another until they make a tapestry that your eye cannot hold.
The guilds of Rimmen are seven because the Weaver was seven weavers. They argued and quit, and the dead have kept the pattern since. Do not copy it hastily, walker. It does not like hurry.
mq_els_rim_cellar: The cellar is cold and silent. At the far end, between two barrels, a grey figure sits with its hands folded and its face turned up to the dripping ceiling.
When the first tile slides into place the dripping stops, and the figure nods once, slowly, and fades like breath on a mirror.
mq_els_dune_wreck: Seven wagons stand in a circle on a salt-crust flat. The sand has drifted to the axles, and the draft-cats lie curled in their harness as if asleep. They are not asleep.
Seven wagons, and the eighth driver was Mizra's own cousin. Look. No claw-marks, no fire. Just the water barrels split along the staves, all at once, as if a hand had squeezed them.
mq_els_hak_align: The ring of moonstones stands silent. Then, between one breath and the next, both moons rise at once above the same stone, and a thin silver line runs from the third stone to the ground at your feet.
There. Hold the lens still. Do not breathe. The line points to a door. The door has not been seen in eleven hundred years, and it will not be seen again until the moons come together.

quests.title: The Lunar Ledger
quests.offer: Why does a scribe look so unhappy at a column of numbers?
quests.pitch: Because the column is wrong by one, walker. One cask in every moon-cycle, for a year. The temple blesses four hundred, the Exchange receives three hundred ninety-nine. Jaro has checked the scales, the ink, his own eyes. The cask is going somewhere between the shrine and the Exchange, and the road is not long enough to hide a cask.
quests.desc: Mane's Scribe Jaro of Torval cannot make the moon-sugar ledger balance: one blessed cask disappears every lunar cycle between the temple and the Exchange.

objectives.text: Read the tally-stones at the Shrine of the Twin Moons
Wait for night, when the stones record both moons' marks
Drive off the squatters at the Temple of the Purifying Moons
Take the temple's tally-stone
Show Ri'dar the two columns of notches
objectives.topic: The temple counts four hundred out. Your scales count three ninety-nine in. Look at the stone.
objectives.reply: Ri'dar turns the disc over twice and sets it down very gently, the way one handles a sleeping wasp. "Then it is not the scales. Then it is the road. Or someone who knows the road. Ri'dar will say nothing in the Exchange. Do you want the Mane told, or do you want the cask found first?"

choices.label: Tell the Mane's Court at once. A theft is a theft.
choices.reply: Ri'dar nods slowly. "Then Shahra will sing it at the hour of Secunda. Loudly. The thief will know before you do. Go with your claws out."

choices.label: Find the cask first. A quiet thief makes a mistake.
choices.reply: Ri'dar almost smiles. "Good. Quiet. Walk the sugar roads at night, where the casks go. Ri'dar will keep the stone and an empty face."

quests.outro: The stone was clear: the road itself had a mouth in it. The only question was who fed it, and where they kept what they swallowed.

quests.title: The Cask That Walks
quests.desc: The missing cask leaves a trail of sugar-dust along the caravan road to the Sugar-Slingers' Den. Ma'rish Half-Tail has been lending blessed sugar to strangers.

objectives.text: Follow the sugar-dust trail along Red Hand's Run
Watch the caravan road at night, where the casks change carts
Find the Sugar-Slingers' Den
Settle accounts with Ma'rish Half-Tail
Bring Ma'rish's tab-book to Jaro
objectives.topic: Here is where the cask went. All four hundred of them, one a moon.
objectives.reply: Jaro reads three lines and goes grey to the ears. "The Purring Ledger's tab-book. Ma'tisha's own hand. But the pawprints here are not hers, walker; they are Ri'dar's. Or they are very cleverly Ri'dar's. What does one do with a thief who is also the man who counted for him?"

choices.label: Declare it. The Mane should know a warden was bought.
choices.reply: Jaro unrolls a clean sheet. "Then it is written. Shahra will have a new verse by moonrise, and Ri'dar a long night. Torval will remember you kindly, and him less so."

choices.label: Burn the page. Ma'rish is dead, and the road is honest again.
choices.reply: Jaro feeds the page to the lamp. "Then the ledger balances at last, and nobody will know why. Ri'dar will weigh honest for the rest of his life, out of fright. That is not nothing."

quests.outro: One cask per moon had walked all the way from the temple to a den in the dunes. The ledger now balances, and what that cost is for the chooser to carry.

quests.title: The Unsung Hour
quests.offer: You sing the hours. Is one of them giving you trouble?
quests.pitch: One hour, walker. The hour when neither moon is up. Shahra has sung it every night for nine years, and last week she opened her mouth and nothing came. Not stage-fright. Nothing. The old song-keepers say the hour has to be paid for, with a verse, to the dead who first sang it.
quests.desc: Court Singer Shahra has lost her voice for the hour when neither moon is up. She must find the first singers of that hour, buried in the ossuary east of Torval.

objectives.text: Travel to the Tenarr Zalviit Ossuary
Quiet the restless dead of the ossuary
Silence the Hollow Choirmaster who sings the hour wrongly
Tell Shahra what you found in the ossuary
objectives.topic: The first singers of the dark hour are not at rest. Someone has been conducting them.
objectives.reply: Shahra's hand goes to her throat, and then she laughs once, low. "A conductor. Of course. Someone made the hour sing for them. Then the hour had nothing left for me. Will you teach it back its own song? Or shall Shahra take a new hour and let that one lie?"

choices.label: Sing it the old verse yourself, Shahra. It remembers you.
choices.reply: Shahra stands. Her voice is rough, then clear, then terrible and lovely. The lamps in the Court gutter and steady. "There. It sang back. You are in the song now, walker, in the second line."

choices.label: Let it rest. Choose a new hour, one nobody owns.
choices.reply: Shahra bows her head. "A sad answer. A good one. There is an hour at dawn that no one has ever sung. Shahra will have it, and give you the first verse."

quests.outro: The ossuary's dead were conducting themselves, in the end, by habit. Shahra has her voice, and the hour of the held breath has a verse for you.

quests.title: The Wager of the Purring Ledger
quests.offer: Your tab-book looks heavier than it should be.
quests.pitch: Ah, a clever one. Ma'tisha took a wager, you see. With a caravan-master from Rimmen. Whoever carries a full cup of moon-sugar-wine from the Purring Ledger to the Hall of the Lunar Champion in Rimmen, without spilling a drop and without a drop of help, wins eleven tabs wiped clean. Ma'tisha is too round to run. You are not.
quests.desc: Ma'tisha of the Purring Ledger wants a cup of moon-sugar-wine carried unspilled from Torval to the Hall of the Lunar Champion in Rimmen, across a road that does not like cups.

objectives.text: Carry the cup across the sandy road to the Sugar Bowl at Rimmen
Do not rest. Arrive after dusk, when the cup is coldest
Set the cup at the feet of the Lunar Champion's statue
Tell Ma'tisha the cup arrived whole
objectives.topic: The cup arrived. Not a drop spilled. A statue drank some, though.
objectives.reply: Ma'tisha laughs until she has to hold the bar. "A statue drank some! Then the caravan-master owes ME. Eleven tabs wiped, and one drink on the house for as long as you live, walker. Ma'tisha means it, which is the terrible part."

quests.outro: Eleven tabs were wiped clean in Torval that evening, and one stranger was entered in the Purring Ledger with no paw-print at all, which is the highest honour the house gives.

quests.title: A Pattern from Below
quests.offer: You have the look of an artisan who has lost something.
quests.pitch: Not lost, walker. Mislaid by my teacher's teacher, who took it into the necropolis with him in a funeral shroud. A pattern. A way of weaving seven strands into one cloth that does not tear, and Kahlil has a Prince's commission he cannot fill without it. The pattern is on the necropolis wall, painted by the dead. Only Sira can open the door, and Sira does not like Kahlil. She might like you.
quests.desc: Master Artisan Kahlil needs a lost seven-strand weaving pattern that is painted on a mural in the Rimmen necropolis. Gatewarden Sira holds the key.

objectives.text: Ask Gatewarden Sira for the key to the necropolis
objectives.topic: Kahlil wants a pattern from the mural. I would like to look at it, with your leave.
objectives.reply: Sira weighs you for a long, quiet moment. "He wants it for a commission. The dead have no commission. But the pattern was woven by one of them, and I think she would like to be seen again. Take the key. Bring it back before the second moon sets, and keep your lamp covered."

objectives.text: Open the necropolis gate and descend
Fight your way through the lower galleries to the mural hall
Face the Weaver Who Would Not Stop at the mural
Take the rubbing to Kahlil, or to whoever deserves it
objectives.topic: I have your pattern. Seven strands, one cloth. Before I give it, who is it for?
objectives.reply: Kahlil reaches for the silk and stops himself, which costs him visibly. "For the Prince's commission. For the guild. For Rimmen, even. Kahlil would like to say for himself, and does not, which you may count as a small virtue. What will you do with what the dead made?"

choices.label: Give it to Kahlil. A master should wear the cloth of his craft.
choices.reply: Kahlil bows lower than a man of his rank ought. "Then the Prince will have his commission, and every apprentice in Rimmen will learn to weave seven strands as one. You have done Rimmen a great kindness."

choices.label: Give it to Prince-Advisor Lek, for all seven guilds to share.
choices.reply: Kahlil's mouth tightens, and then he laughs. "Seven guilds will argue over it for a generation. That is how the Weaver died. But it is yours to give, and Kahlil will learn it from the copies like everyone else."

choices.label: Return it. Hang it back in the dark where the Weaver can see it.
choices.reply: Kahlil closes his eyes. "Foolish. Noble. The sort of thing the dead understand. Very well. Rimmen will weave what it can without it. Kahlil owes you a debt, though he would rather not."

quests.outro: The seven strands of the Weaver's pattern are known again, or buried again. Either way Rimmen has an artisan in its debt and a gatewarden who has stopped scowling at you.

quests.title: The Dead Pay No Rent
quests.offer: Is something wrong with the wine again, Tamhir?
quests.pitch: No, walker, worse. The wine is fine. It is the cellar. Every night something sits at the end of the cellar and does not drink, just stares at the barrels. Tamhir has been to the Masterworks on the cliff, where the tomb-masons come up for air, and they say it is a prior tenant. The cellar was a tomb-vestibule once. The tenant has been complaining of damp.
quests.desc: Tamhir's cellar has a silent visitor: a long-dead tenant of the old tomb-vestibule under the Sugar Bowl. The Masterworks may know what it wants.

objectives.text: Ask Kahlil in the Masterworks who the tomb-vestibule was built for
objectives.topic: The cellar under the Sugar Bowl has a dead tenant. Do the masons keep a roll of who is buried there?
objectives.reply: Kahlil rolls his eyes and finds a ledger anyway. "A tomb-mason's wife, Mirra-jo. The mason ran off with a Baandari caravan and left her under the floor of a half-built vault. The roll says she wanted a roof over her. Not her grave. A roof. Her grave is fine. It is the roof that leaks."

objectives.text: Fetch the lead-and-tile roofing the Masterworks keeps for the dead
Return to the Sugar Bowl cellar after dark
Tell Tamhir the cellar will be dry by morning
objectives.topic: The tenant is satisfied. The roof is mended. She asks that you do not water the wine.
objectives.reply: Tamhir covers his heart with both paws. "Water the wine! After this? She will be the first guest to leave a tip. Walker, the Sugar Bowl owes you a night, a bed, and a cup of the good stuff, which is the stuff that is not the house wine."

quests.outro: A tomb-mason's wife has her roof at last, and the Sugar Bowl's cellar has never been so well kept. Tamhir swears the wine tastes better, and has never again been seen to water it.

quests.title: The Champion's Challenge
quests.offer: The Prince's advisor wants a champion of his own, I hear.
quests.pitch: Not for himself, walker. For the Hall of the Lunar Champion. Every Midyear the hall sets a challenge, and the winner's name is cut into the pillar. This year the other three challengers are the Prince's nephew, a Baandari duellist who has never lost, and a very large cat from Torval. Lek would very much like none of them to win, for reasons of diplomacy. You are a stranger, which is to say, unbought.
quests.desc: Prince-Advisor Lek wants an unbought stranger to win this year's challenge at the Hall of the Lunar Champion, so that none of the rival factions gains the pillar.

objectives.text: Enter the challenge at the Hall of the Lunar Champion
Defeat the Baandari duellist Ri'zhar Never-Lost
Tell Lek the pillar bears your name
objectives.topic: It is done. The pillar says what I am. Whose banner do I carry in this?
objectives.reply: Lek tilts his head, calculating. "None. That is exactly the thing. The nephew will sulk, the Baandari will bow, and Torval will send a very large cat to be offended. Walker, name one thing Rimmen can do for you that a banner would have bought, and we shall pretend we are friends."

choices.label: A road-pass. Rimmen's caravan roads, unquestioned, for a year.
choices.reply: Lek writes it in a clean hand and seals it with a ring. "A road is a good thing to want. It is nearly the same as a friend."

choices.label: Nothing. Let the pillar be what it is.
choices.reply: Lek stares. Then, slowly, bows with all the grace his office allows. "That is the rarest answer in this city. The pillar is yours, and the Prince shall hear of you."

quests.outro: The pillar bears a stranger's name for a year. Three factions grumbled, and one advisor slept very well.

quests.title: The Bitter Batch
quests.offer: Your arms are burned, but your face looks sicker.
quests.pitch: The batch, walker. Third floor, vat Four-Fingers. Every sack she brews tastes right and sits wrong. Dockhands who eat it get slow and sweet-eyed, then they forget where their boats are. It is not my sugar. Tema would taste it blind. Someone is putting something in after the boil, and Tema cannot prove it. She can only make you taste three batches and tell her which one tastes honest.
quests.desc: Boiler Tema says someone is tainting finished sugar after the boil. She needs a stranger's tongue to judge three batches and trace the bad one.

objectives.text: Taste the three batches Tema sets before you
objectives.topic: Three plates, three sugars. I taste them in order. Which one is wrong?
objectives.reply: Tema watches you chew with the intensity of a cat at a mousehole. "The second. Yes. You see? Sweet, then iron, then a long cold nothing. That batch left Sugar Boil House yesterday on cart-nine for the quay. Find cart-nine."

objectives.text: Search Senchal Merchant Square for the nine-wheeled sugar cart
Ask Ja'khar about cart-nine's customs stamp
objectives.topic: Customs-Master, a sugar cart stamped nine passed your quay yesterday. Who paid its toll?
objectives.reply: Ja'khar pulls a ledger and reads without hurry. "Nine. Stamped by... Rhal, the Prince's cousin, for a private lading to the black-hulled ship at the Black Kiergo. Ja'khar does not ask what a Prince's cousin carries. It is bad for the lungs."

objectives.text: Climb down to the Black Kiergo and watch the black-hulled ship
Confront Zahra the Bitter-Hand, the dealer who taints sugar
Return Tema's token and tell her what you found
objectives.topic: The token was in a vat that was not yours. Zahra paid a boiler to tip a powder in after the boil.
objectives.reply: Tema holds the brass token as if it were still hot. "Pali. Fourth floor. Tema trained her. Fed her. She will do it again if no one speaks to her. What should Tema do with a girl who poisoned a thousand sacks for a handful of silver?"

choices.label: Give her the sluice again. She did it because she was afraid.
choices.reply: Tema is quiet. "Then Tema will be afraid for her. A boiler who remembers is a better boiler. You are not a gentle soul, walker, but you are kind."

choices.label: Turn her in. She sold her vat, and cost a hundred their wits.
choices.reply: Tema nods once, hard. "Then it is done properly. The Customs-Master will be there at dawn. Tema will stir her vats and not look at the fourth floor."

quests.outro: The Bitter Batch was a poison with a name, a face and a price. Senchal's sugar is clean again, and its boilers are warier of strangers who offer silver.

quests.title: A Favour for the Prince's Cousin
quests.offer: You have the look of a person who might help the Prince's family.
quests.pitch: The Prince's cousin! Yes! You are so sharp. Rhal has a very small favour. A rival of his, a wool factor, is about to sail to Rimmen with a cargo that would, shall we say, embarrass Rhal at a banquet. If the ship were simply... slow. A day. Two. Nothing criminal. Just the kind of delay that happens to ships. Rhal would pay.
quests.desc: The Prince's cousin Rhal wants a rival's ship delayed in the harbour, without anyone knowing it was done on purpose.

objectives.text: Visit the Senchal Customs House and read the sailing roll
Ask Ja'khar when the wool factor's ship will sail
objectives.topic: The wool factor's ship. Rhal wants her... slow. Is there a customs reason she might be?
objectives.reply: Ja'khar takes off his spectacles slowly. "There is always a customs reason, walker. Ja'khar will find one. And he will find, in the same breath, that the cargo of the cousin's own ship is carrying more than its manifest. Which of the two inspections would you like to see happen first?"

choices.label: Delay the wool factor, as Rhal asks. A favour is a favour.
choices.reply: Ja'khar scratches a note. "Then the wool will sit three days for a stamp that has been lost. Ja'khar has done worse for less, and not enjoyed it."

choices.label: Inspect the cousin's ship instead. Let the manifest speak.
choices.reply: Ja'khar's ears go forward with something like joy. "Ah! Ja'khar has wanted to open those barrels for a year. Tell the cousin nothing. Let him find out in public."

objectives.text: Report to Rhal
objectives.topic: It is done. You will hear about it by evening.
objectives.reply: Rhal beams like a man who has already forgotten he asked. "Marvellous! You are an ornament to Senchal. The Prince shall hear of you. Or perhaps he shall hear of me. Either way, you are paid, and I am delighted, and the wool is somebody's problem."

quests.outro: Some favours leave a taste, and some leave a ledger entry. In Senchal it is generally both.

quests.title: The Wind That Pays for Glass
quests.offer: Another broken window, Zhaleh?
quests.pitch: The ninth this winter, walker, and every one of them on the third floor, and every one of them at the same hour. The wind does not do that. Wind is a coward. It comes in whichever hole it finds. This one comes in at the same bay window, in the same shape, with a smell of old rope. I would wager my best pillow someone is coming through that window, and someone has been, for nine nights.
quests.desc: Zhaleh's inn, the Sweet Breezes, loses a window every night at the same hour. She suspects the culprit is no wind at all.

objectives.text: Keep watch in the third-floor room until the window breaks
Catch the intruder who climbs in through the bay window
Tell Zhaleh who was breaking the glass
objectives.topic: It was a rope-climbing burglar in a bay-window-sized hurry. The wind is innocent.
objectives.reply: Zhaleh blinks and then bursts into delighted laughter. "The wind is innocent! I have been scolding it for a month! I have been leaving it apologies on the sill! Walker, you have saved a poor old sea-breeze its good name."

quests.outro: The Sweet Breezes' bay window is whole, and a wind that had never done anything wrong now gets a saucer of milk on the sill each evening.

quests.title: The Missing Caravan
quests.offer: You are a driver who has lost wagons.
quests.pitch: Seven, walker. Left the Wheel ten days ago for the Temar oasis, and the oasis never saw them. Mizra drove that road for twenty years. Between here and there the only things that kill a caravan are thirst, bandits and a very bad mood, and none of those leave no bodies. Find them. Find the eighth driver, who is Mizra's cousin, and who always carried a bell.
quests.desc: Seven wagons of a Dune caravan never reached the Temar oasis. Camel-Driver Mizra wants to know what happened to them, and to her cousin, the eighth driver.

objectives.text: Check Nevoe Oasis, the first water on the Temar road
Follow the wheel-ruts to Teal Campsite
Find the eighth driver's bell among the wagons
Clear the poachers off Temar Oasis
Face Zhirr the Oasis-Snatcher, who dammed the well
Bring the bell back to Mizra
objectives.topic: Your cousin's bell. Zhirr dammed the well and let the caravan die of thirst. Your cousin tied the clapper so the bell wouldn't call him back.
objectives.reply: Mizra holds the bell to her ear and nothing rings. "He tied it. The fool tied it so the wagons would not wake the thieves. It cost him his life and saved the camels. Mizra will carry it to the Wheel and hang it at the eighth lane. The Eighth Spoke is named for him, you know. Nobody remembers."

choices.label: Tell the Wheel what Zhirr did. Let Khir hunt his gang.
choices.reply: Mizra nods. "Then every cart on the Wheel will remember. The Wheel-Master will send riders. There will be a day of drums for the eight."

choices.label: Keep the story quiet. The families have grieved enough.
choices.reply: Mizra wipes her eyes with her wrist. "Then it stays with the bell. A kindness, and a hard one. Take the road-pass; no toll on any lane, for as long as Mizra drives."

quests.outro: Seven wagons and an eighth driver went to their rest at last, and a bell with a tied clapper hangs where only camel-drivers look.

quests.title: The Knot That Is Not Khir's
quests.offer: Something is wrong with your toll-tally.
quests.pitch: You see it too! One knot, walker. Blue thread, tied right-over-left. Khir ties left-over-right, always, since he was a cub. Someone has tied a toll that Khir did not take, for a cart Khir did not see. A hundred knots, and one of them is not his. Find the cart that paid a toll that was never collected.
quests.desc: One knot in Wheel-Master Khir's toll-tally is tied by a stranger's hand. He wants the cart behind it found.

objectives.text: Ask Water-Seller Hajir who passes the hub at night
objectives.topic: A blue-thread knot on Khir's tally. Who passes the hub after the Wheel-Master has gone to bed?
objectives.reply: Hajir looks left, right, and then at his barrel. "A cart. With a cloth over it. Every ninth night, gone by dawn. Hajir sold its driver three cups, and he paid with a coin so old it had a prince on it who is not a prince any more."

objectives.text: Stand watch at the hub of the Wheel until the cloth-covered cart appears
Stop the cloth-covered cart at the Sugar Stack Mart
Tell Khir who tied the blue knot
objectives.topic: The knot was tied by a hauler who pays you in old coin to keep the hub quiet. He is stopped.
objectives.reply: Khir stares at the coin you give him and for once says nothing. "Old Prince's coin. Khir's own father took those. The knot was Khir's father's way of tying. He taught it to a nephew. The nephew... Walker, it seems the Wheel has been paying a debt that Khir did not know he owed."

quests.outro: The blue knot is still in Khir's tally. He says he will leave it there to remember by.

quests.title: Nuri Tells Too Much
quests.offer: Your cards look very tired.
quests.pitch: They are, walker. Nuri told a customer yesterday exactly how he would die, and he paid in a very large bag and left, and the bag was full of sand. Now there is a rider outside the tent who says he knows which of her cards is true. Nuri would prefer to hear it from a better liar than herself.
quests.desc: Nuri the fortune-teller has been paid in sand and is being watched by a rider who claims to know which of her cards is true.

objectives.text: Confront the rider who watches Nuri's tent
Tell Nuri what the rider carried
objectives.topic: The rider carried a sealed letter. He was paid to see whether your cards ever lie.
objectives.reply: Nuri reads the letter and folds it in four with delicate paws. "Ah. A rival. Someone in Rimmen sells fortunes and has lost a customer. Nuri is flattered. Take this card, walker. The Tower. It will not mean what you think. It will mean exactly what you do next."

quests.outro: The rider's letter is now a bookmark in Nuri's book of true cards, and a Rimmen fortune-teller has an enemy for life.

quests.title: The Wheel That Would Not Turn
quests.desc: The eighth driver's bell started something. A bone-pale warden has risen in the dunes north of Dune to demand the toll that his own prince promised him a thousand years ago.

objectives.text: Cross the Hill of Shattered Swords where the warden is said to walk
Wait for night. The warden walks only by moonlight
Put the Sand-Sworn Warden to rest
Tell Khir the warden is at rest
objectives.topic: A warden walked the dunes demanding a toll the prince promised. I paid it in the only coin he understood.
objectives.reply: Khir presses the tally to his chest. "A toll. A thousand years. And you paid it. The Wheel has never been so quiet. Take this coin. It is the first copper ever struck for the Great Market. Khir has no right to keep it."

quests.outro: The warden's toll is settled. The Great Market Wheel turns, and the eight lanes are quiet at night.

quests.title: The Garden's Bees
quests.offer: Your hives sound unhappy.
quests.pitch: They are not unhappy, walker. They are quiet. Three hundred hives of the Garden Cathedral, and eleven of them have fallen silent in a week. A quiet hive is a hive without a queen. The Cathedral's oldest queen was carried out by a stranger in the night, and Mura thinks the stranger took her to the old arch above the canals, where the wild hornets nest. Bring her back, or at least bring back what she was carrying.
quests.desc: Gardener-Priest Mura says the Garden Cathedral's oldest queen bee has been carried off to the hornet-haunted arch above the canals.

objectives.text: Climb to Khenarthi's Arch above the canals
Kill the Hornet-Queen that has taken the old queen's hive
Take the queen cell from the hornet nest
Carry the queen cell to Mura without jostling it
objectives.topic: The old queen's cell, whole. Where would you like it to wake?
objectives.reply: Mura's veil trembles. "Wake? She will wake where she is welcomed. Put her in the hive nearest the bell, and bless her with the first honey of the morning. There are eleven hives that need her more than I need to say thank you."

choices.label: Put her in the Cathedral's hive, where she was born.
choices.reply: Mura nods. "The old way. The hive will remember her, and she will remember it. The eleven quiet ones will sing again by Fredas."

choices.label: Split the cell. Let the eleven quiet hives each have a share.
choices.reply: Mura laughs, startled. "Eleven queens from one! The old priests would have fainted. It is a risk, and a good one. Walker, you think like a beekeeper."

quests.outro: The Garden Cathedral hums again. The first honey of the season has a faint taste of something that no flower in Corinthe has ever worn.

quests.title: The Canal Regatta
quests.offer: You hum off-key as a duty, Boatman?
quests.pitch: Ajh is the best boatman in Corinthe and the worst singer. At midsummer there is a regatta, and Ajh has entered, and someone has sawn through his pole three nights in a row. Ajh would like to win, but more than winning, Ajh would like to know who is so afraid of a man who hums off-key. Sit in the boat. Watch the bridges. Bring a very sharp eye.
quests.desc: Someone has been sabotaging Boatman Ajh's pole before the midsummer regatta. He needs a watcher in the boat and an eye on the bridges.

objectives.text: Hide in the boat shed and wait for the saboteur
Catch the pole-saboteur at the canal stairs
Tell Ajh who wanted him to lose
objectives.topic: The saboteur was paid by a rival boatman who cannot stand your singing. He is caught.
objectives.reply: Ajh bursts out laughing so hard the boat rocks. "My singing! He sawed my pole because of my singing! Walker, I will win the regatta now just to sing the victory song louder at him."

quests.outro: Corinthe's regatta was the loudest in years. A boatman sang off-key through all of it, and the sawyer sat in the stands and was forced to listen.

quests.title: The Pear That Wasn't There
quests.offer: Your grafting-book is locked. Is something missing from it?
quests.pitch: A pear, walker. A white pear that does not exist in any orchard in Pellitine. Twenty years ago Zhel grafted it from a branch a Khajiit pilgrim brought down from the Halls of Colossus, and it fruited once, and tasted of every season at once. Then the tree died. Someone has been selling cuttings in Valenwood as "Corinthe white". Zhel did not sell them. Zhel did not keep a cutting.
quests.desc: Matron Zhel's extinct white pear is being sold as cuttings in Valenwood, though she never kept one. Someone stole it from her grafting-book.

objectives.text: Ask after the pear at the Halls of Colossus, where the branch was found
Clear the machines that guard the colossus hall
Recover the pilgrim's cog, which hides the grafting notes
Catch Orlin Quick-Shears, the grafting-book thief
Bring Zhel the cog and the news
objectives.topic: The pear was copied from your grafting-book by Orlin. I found the pilgrim's original notes, too.
objectives.reply: Zhel unfolds the notes with trembling fingers. "Every season at once. Zhel did not know the pilgrim wrote it down. Walker, you have brought back a recipe, not a pear. It is the better gift. Do you want your name on the first branch, or should Zhel hide it, as hiding has been her way?"

choices.label: Put my name on it. Corinthe should know the pear's true grafter.
choices.reply: Zhel sniffs, moved. "A small tag, then. 'Gift of a stranger'. It will be printed on every crate."

choices.label: Hide it in your book again. Some pears are meant to be rare.
choices.reply: Zhel closes the book with great gentleness. "Rare. Yes. That is the word the pilgrim used, too."

quests.outro: A pear that tastes of every season is a secret of Corinthe again, or a gift for all of Pellitine. Zhel's book, at least, is safe.

quests.title: The Dry Season
quests.offer: Your cisterns look full to me.
quests.pitch: They look full, walker. But Mala has counted every drop for thirty years, and the Third Cistern is lower by a barrel every fourth night. There is no leak. Mala has been down the shaft with a torch and a rope. Something is taking it, cleanly, the way a cat takes cream. Raz will not believe it. Raz believes only what he can hit.
quests.desc: Cistern-Keeper Mala says a barrel is stolen from Orcrest's Third Cistern every fourth night, with no leak and no mark.

objectives.text: Inspect the rooftop cisterns of Orcrest
Hide in the Third Cistern's shaft until the water-thief comes
Follow the wet rope-marks to the Scar and recover the cracked seal
Corner Thirst-Lord Zadhir in Talon Gulch
Show Raz the cracked seal and tell him of the thief
objectives.topic: The water was being hauled out through a cut in the seal by a thief who sells it back to you. Zadhir is dead.
objectives.reply: Raz looks at the seal for a long time. "Sold back. To us. Water we owned." He does not smile, but his jaw does something close. "Mala was right. Raz will say it once. Mala was right. The Gate will open a morning early for you, any time, any day."

quests.outro: Orcrest's Third Cistern stays full. Mala keeps counting. Raz, grudgingly, keeps a chair for her at the Gate.

quests.title: The Gate That Hums
quests.offer: You are watching something, Scout.
quests.pitch: The Gate, walker. Hear it? On the first night of the dry wind, the Claw Gate hums. Raz says it is the stone cooling. Sihe was born in the watchtower. It is not the stone. It is a note, and the note is under the plateau, and every time it sounds the sand on the south road shivers, as if there is a drum beneath it. Go to the shrine to Lorkhaj on the edge of the mesa. It is the oldest hearing-place Sihe knows.
quests.desc: Scout Sihe hears a deep note under Orcrest every dry-wind night. She wants someone to listen from the old shrine to Lorkhaj.

objectives.text: Listen for the hum at the shrine to Lorkhaj
Wait for the dry wind to rise after dusk
Silence what drums beneath the plateau in the Bone Pit
Tell Sihe the hum has stopped
objectives.topic: A drum-priest was beating the dead beneath the plateau. The note is gone. Listen.
objectives.reply: Sihe tilts her ears and stays very still for a long moment. "Nothing. The Gate is quiet. Sihe has not heard the plateau be quiet since she was a cub. It is... lonely. Thank you, walker. Sihe will miss it, which is not at all what she expected."

quests.outro: The Claw Gate no longer hums at night, and Sihe, who could hear it from the top of the world, has begun to sleep in the afternoons.

quests.title: Moon Alignment
quests.offer: Your ring of stones seems to be watching me.
quests.pitch: It is watching all of us, walker. Once in a long time the moons stand over the same stone, and a tomb below Hakoshae opens for a night. The Guardians keep the key; the Ring-Keeper keeps the hour. This is that hour. Su'ri cannot go alone, for the Guardians do not leave the ring. Take the lens. Hold the line. Carry the light to the tomb.
quests.desc: Ring-Keeper Dar says the moons will align over the third stone of Hakoshae tonight. A lens carried to the tomb below may open it.

objectives.text: Ask Guardian Su'ri for the Alignment Lens
objectives.topic: Dar says the hour is tonight. He says you keep the lens. May I take it?
objectives.reply: Su'ri weighs the lens in her palm and then lets it fall into yours, like trusting a bird. "A hard thing to give. Guardians do not leave the ring, and the lens has never left the ring either. It is your hour now. Mind the line. Mind your breath."

objectives.text: Wait in the ring until both moons stand over the third stone
Carry the lens's line to the Hakoshae Tombs
Face the Tenant Beneath the Third Stone
Return the lens to Dar
objectives.topic: The tomb is closed again. The tenant is at rest. Here is the lens.
objectives.reply: Dar takes the lens, holds it up to the dawn, and sees nothing. "Good. Empty. The line is spent. The moons will not stand over that stone again for a century. Do you wish the lens placed in the ring, to point the way for the next Keeper? Or taken on your road, in case another door opens?"

choices.label: Place it in the ring. The next Keeper will need it.
choices.reply: Dar settles the lens into a hollow in the third stone as if it were always meant to go there. "Then it waits. The ring thanks you. So do we all."

choices.label: Keep it. Another door may open somewhere.
choices.reply: Dar bows his head. "Then you are the Keeper now, a little. Go gently. The moons are not always kind to those who carry their light."

quests.outro: The ring of moonstones is quiet. The tomb below it has closed its door for a hundred years, and its tenant, at last, rests on the other side of the stone.

quests.title: The Pilgrim Who Would Not Finish
quests.offer: Your seventeenth bed is empty tonight.
quests.pitch: It is, walker, and Hamza does not like it. Ke the pilgrim left four days ago for the Shrine of the Crescent. He always returns the same night, because he walks in loops. He has not. Ke is a gentle fool, and the road to the shrine is not gentle.
quests.desc: Pilgrim Ke has not returned from the Shrine of the Crescent, and Hamza fears the worst.

objectives.text: Search the Shrine of the Crescent for Pilgrim Ke
Drive off the bandits who have made camp at the shrine
Escort Pilgrim Ke back to Hakoshae

quests.outro: Ke was found asleep in a bandit's bedroll, quite content, with a bandit's hat on. He says he has begun a third lap. Hamza says that is a lie.

quests.title: A Story for a Ride
quests.offer: Is that a netch you fly?
quests.pitch: A balloon, walker. Grown from a netch's sac. Q'ri trades rides for stories, and she is out of stories she has not told. So: Q'ri will give you a ride to anywhere you like, if you bring her one story that she has never heard. Something that happened. Not something you made up. She can tell.
quests.desc: Balloonist Q'ri will trade a ride for a true story she has never heard. The Hill of Shattered Swords might provide one.

objectives.text: Walk the Hill of Shattered Swords and see what it says
Find the Shrine of the Cats Divine
Tell Q'ri what you saw
objectives.topic: There is a hill planted with broken swords, and a shrine of giant cats watching it. The swords hum when the wind passes.
objectives.reply: Q'ri puts down her cup and stares. "Hums? She has been to the hill, and never once heard it hum. It hums for those who walk it. She will give you a ride, walker. And Q'ri will go walk the hill herself. That is the best thing you could have given her: a reason to go."

quests.outro: Q'ri took the long way round to the hill, and did not come back for a week. She says it hums quite beautifully.

quests.title: Who Burned the Cane
quests.offer: The ash is cold. Whose fire was it?
quests.pitch: Not lightning. Not lamp. The fire began in four corners at once, in the dark of the new moon, and the wind that night was from the west, which would have pushed the fire back on itself. Four hands set it. Four people who know Tathara's fields. She does not wish to name them. She would be very happy for you to.
quests.desc: Tathara's sugar fields were set alight from four corners at once. She does not want to name the neighbours she suspects.

objectives.text: Search the burned fields for the fire-setters' tracks
Catch the arsonists at Hanikhi Outpost
Tell Tathara who hired the fire
objectives.topic: Four hired hands, paid by a buyer who wanted your land for his own cane. He is a neighbour. You may guess which.
objectives.reply: Tathara closes her eyes. "Guessed. Always guessed. The one with the new gate. The one who brought pies at the funeral of the crop. Walker, there will be a reckoning, and it will not be with fire. Tathara will plant again. She will plant it twice as wide, right up to his gate."

quests.outro: Tathara's new cane stands close to a neighbour's fence, uncomfortably tall, and sweet as anything.

quests.title: The Star-Chart That Left Early
quests.offer: Your ceiling-tiles seem well counted.
quests.pitch: They are. Three hundred and nine. Walker, a star-chart of the winter sky has left the lectern, and with it the only record Zhazir has of the seventh moon, which his old tutor swore appeared once in a century above the Starlight Adeptorium. The chart did not walk. It was taken. Someone with a very good hand for silver ink.
quests.desc: A star-chart showing a rumoured seventh moon has vanished from the star-haven lectern. The Starlight Adeptorium may know who wanted it.

objectives.text: Ask at the Starlight Adeptorium who copies star-charts in silver ink
Catch the copyist on the Saimisil Steppes
Return the star-chart to Zhazir
objectives.topic: Your chart. The copyist sold copies to three rival adeptoria. The seventh moon is the same in each. It seems not to be a joke.
objectives.reply: Zhazir unfolds the chart and stares at the faint pencil moon for a long time. "Seven. Not six. Not two plus a ghost. Seven. His tutor was not mad. Zhazir will not say this to the cubs. He will only look at the sky and count."

quests.outro: A seventh moon waits in pencil under the winter stars. Zhazir counts it every night, though no one else will say they see it.

quests.title: The Route Book of Ha'bir
quests.offer: A route book is a heavy loss for a trader.
quests.pitch: It is worth a clan, walker. It lists every well, every ambush and every price. Ha'bir does not ask for the thief's head. He asks that you take back the book before someone sells a Baandari route to a rival clan. There is a camp west of here, Nekha, where bad men buy and good men look the other way.
quests.desc: Route-Master Ha'bir's Baandari route book was stolen. A fence at Nekha Camp is the likeliest buyer.

objectives.text: Find the fence at Nekha Camp
Take the route book from the fence
Return the book to Ha'bir
objectives.topic: Your book, whole. The fence had not yet sold it. He had copied three pages.
objectives.reply: Ha'bir counts the pages with his thumb and breathes out slowly. "Three copied. Three pages. Ha'bir will change those wells by morning. A route book is only a gift to the person who does not know the road has changed. Walker, the Baandari clans owe you a road-name."

quests.outro: Three pages of the route book had to be made false, and a Baandari clan now has a name, in a code that only they can read, for the person who brought the book home.

quests.title: The Hand You Were Dealt
quests.offer: You keep losing to the sky, Keeper.
quests.pitch: Every time, walker! Every wager. Tonight is the full of Masser and the new of Secunda, and Ma'tir has put her whole cellar on it being the other way round. She is a very bad gambler and a very honest one. A rider from Rimmen has been telling the house a different phase every night. Ma'tir thinks he has been bribing the almanac. Please follow him.
quests.desc: Ma'tir of the Twin Moons keeps losing moon-phase wagers because a Rimmen rider feeds her false almanac phases.

objectives.text: Wait at the Twin Moons until the almanac-rider arrives
Stop the rider and take his bribed almanac
Tell Ma'tir the almanac was bribed
objectives.topic: The rider's almanac was pencilled wrong on purpose. Here is a true one.
objectives.reply: Ma'tir snatches the almanac and checks it against the sky out the window. "WRONG! By a whole phase! Ha! Ha! He has been fleecing me for a year, and I have been blaming the sky!"

quests.outro: Ma'tir now wins her moon-phase wagers about one night in three, and says it is a disgrace to the sky.

quests.title: The Borrowed Banner
quests.offer: Your flagpole is bare, Captain.
quests.pitch: Bare, walker, and Raz will not discuss it in the open air. The Claw Gate banner was lifted in the night by the lads of a hill-village that has never forgiven Orcrest for a lost game of knucklebones. They call it borrowing. Raz calls it a war. He cannot send guards: that makes it a war. A stranger may simply walk in, at night, and walk out again. If the stranger is seen, it was a misunderstanding. If not, it was a miracle.
quests.desc: Rivals from a hill-village stole Orcrest's Claw Gate banner as a prank. Gate-Captain Raz wants a stranger to take it back in the night, quietly.

objectives.text: Scout the hill-village camp in Talon Gulch
Wait for night, when the prank-makers sleep
Take the Claw Gate banner from the rival camp
Slip away from Kasha Hill-Banner, who wakes
Raise the banner over the Claw Gate
objectives.topic: Your banner, whole. The rivals did not do it for malice. They were hoping you would climb the hill to fetch it, and say sorry about the knucklebones.
objectives.reply: Raz looks at the banner a long moment, then at the gate, then, for the first time in your acquaintance, at his own feet. "Knucklebones. Thirty years. Raz cheated, you see. He knew. He has always known. Walker, shall Raz walk up that hill with a cask and an apology, or raise the banner and pretend he has not heard?"

choices.label: Walk up the hill. An old debt is lighter shared.
choices.reply: Raz straightens, almost smiling. "A cask and an apology. And a rematch, at knucklebones, honestly played. Thank you, walker. The gate will be braver for it."

choices.label: Raise the banner and say nothing. Let the prank be the end of it.
choices.reply: Raz nods, and hoists the banner himself. "Then it flies. And the lads on the hill will know they won, quietly, and so will Raz. That is the nicest kind of war."

quests.outro: The Claw Gate banner flies again. A cask went up the hill at dawn with a very polite note, and an old game of knucklebones was, at long last, replayed.

quests.title: The Naming Under Two Moons
quests.offer: Your spear is garlanded with ribbon.
quests.pitch: It is a night for it, walker. A Hakoshae cub is to be named under both moons, and the rite wants a witness who is no kin and has no stake. The mother is ill. The charm has not been blessed. The blessing must be done at the Temple of the Hidden Moon, at the hour both moons stand over its door, and it must be done by a pair of hands that have not held a weapon since dusk. Su'ri cannot lay down her spear. Will you carry the charm?
quests.desc: A Hakoshae cub must be named under both moons. Guardian Su'ri asks a stranger to carry the charm to the Temple of the Hidden Moon for its blessing.

objectives.text: Take the unblessed charm from Su'ri
objectives.topic: I will carry it. Tell me the words of the blessing.
objectives.reply: Su'ri sets the charm in your palm with great care, and looks away, as one does from a thing that is not hers to see. "Two moons, two crescents, one thread. Say the name of the cub when both stand over the door. Do not say it before, and do not say it after. A name said at the wrong hour goes looking for someone else."

objectives.text: Carry the charm to the Temple of the Hidden Moon
Wait in the temple for both moons to stand over the door
Return the blessed charm to Su'ri
objectives.topic: The moons stood over the door. I said the cub's name. The charm is warm. Tie it to her wrist.
objectives.reply: Su'ri takes the charm, and her voice is very low. "Warm. It is warm. The name took. Walker, the mother asks one thing: that the cub's second name be given by you. A cub with a stranger's second name is never lost on a road. What shall it be?"

choices.label: Name her for the road: Ja'hira, 'she who returns'.
choices.reply: Su'ri closes her eyes and says it over, very softly, three times. "Ja'hira. She who returns. It is a good name, and a brave one. Walker, Hakoshae will say it at every doorway."

choices.label: Name her for the stone: Ri'sha, 'she who waits'.
choices.reply: Su'ri smiles into her collar. "Ri'sha. The ring keeps those who wait. It is a gentle name. The mother will weep, and the cub will sleep."

quests.outro: A cub of Hakoshae bears two names, one from her mother and one from a stranger who held a charm and said nothing at the wrong hour.

quests.title: The Resealed Cask
quests.offer: Dar'jazad has a cask that should not be here.
quests.pitch: Not here, no, and not like this, walker. The Moon-Priests' seal is on it, and the seal has been pried and mended with wax. A blessed cask is not to be opened except at the Temple. Someone opened it, took a share, and resealed it badly. Dar'jazad cannot return it to the temple unless the thief is found. A priest's wrath is a gentle thing, until it is not.
quests.desc: A cask of blessed moon-sugar was opened and badly resealed in Senchal. Dar'jazad wants the culprit found before the Moon-Priests notice.

objectives.text: Ask Customs-Master Ja'khar which cart carried the cask
objectives.topic: A blessed cask passed your quay with a broken seal. Whose cart?
objectives.reply: Ja'khar sets down his stamp. "A cask with a pried seal. Stamped by the Warden of the cask-store, one night, Tuesday. A cat with a scar and a very good alibi. Ja'khar has no evidence. He has a strong suspicion, and a tidy mind."

objectives.text: Search the Forgotten Mane, where the cask-store keeps its overflow
Take down the Cask-Warden and recover the stolen share
Return the cask to Dar'jazad
objectives.topic: Your cask, whole. The Warden took a share to sell to a skooma lord. It is returned.
objectives.reply: Dar'jazad turns the cask once and sets it in the lamplight. "The seal is mended. The share is returned. Walker, the Warden is dead, and the Moon-Priests will ask who. Shall Dar'jazad say a thief, or tell the whole tale of the skooma lord, and let the temple deal with it?"

choices.label: Say a thief. The skooma lord can wait.
choices.reply: Dar'jazad nods. "A thief, then. A small lie. It will keep the temple calm, and the lord complacent. We shall see which of us is cleverer."

choices.label: Tell the whole tale. The temple deserves to know.
choices.reply: Dar'jazad exhales. "The whole tale. Then there will be a reckoning, and it will be loud. But the moons love a plain truth, and Senchal has been quiet too long."

quests.outro: A blessed cask was returned to its temple with the seal repaired, and a very quiet skooma lord in Senchal now sleeps rather badly.

quests.title: The Cub Who Read the Ledger
quests.offer: You are a runner of messages.
quests.pitch: Runner, yes! Tazhi has read none of them. All of them. A very long one, today, from the Court to the Exchange, sealed with wax. Tazhi did not break it. The seal broke by itself, when Tazhi sneezed. The note inside says: move the cask at midnight, and the warden will not look. Tazhi did not understand it. Then Tazhi did. Tazhi does not wish to be a cub who knew. Please carry it back, sealed, and say nothing.
quests.desc: Cub-runner Tazhi accidentally read a sealed note ordering a cask moved past a bribed warden. She asks a stranger to return it unread.

objectives.text: Return the note to Mane's Scribe Jaro, resealed
objectives.topic: The cub dropped this. The seal has been mended. I did not read it.
objectives.reply: Jaro takes the note and for a moment says nothing. Then, under his breath: "A cub. A cub, who read it. She is a very honest child, to return it. Walker, the note is not a thing the Court would like to have been read. Tazhi has done right. Jaro will see she is looked after, and a very good, very quiet apprenticeship found."

objectives.text: Tell Tazhi she is safe
objectives.topic: You did right. The scribe is looking after you. Say nothing, and you will be a scribe yourself one day.
objectives.reply: Tazhi's ears flatten with relief, and then rise slowly, slowly. "A scribe! Tazhi has always wanted to be a scribe! But Tazhi will not read any more notes. Not even by accident. Tazhi will sneeze into a handkerchief, like a lady."

quests.outro: A cub of Torval has an apprenticeship at the Lunar Ledger, and a handkerchief, and a great deal of respect for wax.
